content.user_title: Build and Verify Maintainable NestJS Software
content.value_statement: NestJS changes can introduce incompatible syntax, hidden side effects, and public API regressions. This skill guides repository inspection, focused implementation, and evidence-based verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides inspection of repository instructions, installed versions, callers, tests, and existing implementation patterns.
Compares explicit and convenient syntax using installed types, repository conventions, and official version-appropriate documentation.
Directs focused NestJS and TypeScript implementation, debugging, and refactoring while preserving public behavior.
Evaluates API convenience methods for type safety, compatibility, visible side effects, and meaningful caller control.
Selects tests and verification checks according to risk, including authorization, concurrency, persistence, and migration concerns.
Separates read-only review from authorized implementation and reports executed checks separately from remaining assumptions.
limitations: Provides workflow instructions and references, not a bundled NestJS application or executable verification tool.
Requires repository access, compatible tooling, and available services to implement and verify changes.
Cannot guarantee production readiness or claim success for checks that did not run.
Related NestJS skills are optional coordination references and are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Implement an Existing-Service Feature
use_cases.description: Add a NestJS feature using nearby patterns, compatible APIs, focused tests, and clear acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Refine a Public TypeScript API
use_cases.description: Evaluate convenience methods while preserving errors, cancellation, idempotency, and compatibility for existing consumers.

use_cases.title: Review a High-Risk Change
use_cases.description: Inspect behavior and verification gaps without editing files, then distinguish confirmed evidence from assumptions and unavailable checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NestJS service for readability, input validation, and error handling. Inspect nearby conventions and report evidence without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: read-only review of a focused component.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Reproducible Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix [bug] in this NestJS repository. Inspect callers and versions, add a regression test, preserve public behavior, and report executed checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement a bounded fix with regression coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Compatible Convenience API
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [convenience method] alongside the existing explicit API. Compare supported syntax and preserve errors, timeouts, cancellation, and idempotency. Add shared contract tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: reduce repeated API friction without hiding effects.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Cross-Module Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [feature] across these NestJS modules. Map ownership, consumers, authorization, transaction boundaries, and migration risks first. Resolve material conflicts before editing. Report verification gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a high-risk implementation with broader verification.

output_examples.input: Review a proposal that fetches account balances through a property getter.
output: Finding: the getter conceals network I/O, latency, and failure from callers.
Recommendation: use an explicit asynchronous operation with visible timeout and cancellation controls.
Verification plan: cover successful responses, denied access, timeouts, and upstream failures.

output_examples.input: Plan an additive payment capture helper while retaining the explicit execution API.
output: Recommended design: delegate to the existing operation and preserve its result and error contracts.
Caller controls: retain idempotency keys, timeout options, and cancellation behavior.
Compatibility plan: keep both public forms available and test them against the same observable contract.

output_examples.input: Explain verification limits when an integration service is unavailable.
output: Verification boundary: local unit tests and type checks cannot establish external service compatibility.
Remaining evidence: integration and runtime smoke checks require the unavailable service.
Reporting rule: distinguish completed checks from blocked checks and do not report unexecuted checks as passed.

best_practices: Provide acceptance criteria and public compatibility constraints before requesting implementation.
Confirm installed versions and inspect project scripts before selecting syntax or running checks.
Request focused tests first, then expand verification for security, persistence, concurrency, or cross-module changes.
anti_patterns: Copying newer framework syntax without confirming compiler, runtime, and package support.
Hiding network activity, authorization, retries, or state changes behind getters and convenience methods.
Weakening checks or reporting unavailable integration tests as successful.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this package include a NestJS application?
faq.answer: No. It contains workflow instructions, reference guidance, agent configuration, and evaluation scenarios.

faq.question: Can I request a review without file changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow keeps review and diagnosis read-only unless you also authorize implementation.

faq.question: How does it choose TypeScript or NestJS syntax?
faq.answer: It prioritizes repository conventions, installed toolchain evidence, and official documentation for the relevant versions.

faq.question: Are the related NestJS skills required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional ownership references used when installed and relevant to the same decision.

faq.question: What happens when verification cannot run?
faq.answer: The workflow requires reporting blocked checks and missing prerequisites without claiming success or weakening meaningful controls.
